description: Five hooks. (1) PreToolUse on ExitPlanMode — Plan Briefing checkpoint: a deterministic, stateless Node command hook on EVERY ExitPlanMode (Quick Fix Mode and plain plan mode; Spec Mode plans in an ordinary session and never calls ExitPlanMode). It allows (explicitly, see Output below) when a real user reply precedes the call — skipping the agent's mechanical tool turns (e.g. the ToolSearch that loads a deferred ExitPlanMode, a post-approval Edit) so they do not break the check — and blocks a straight planning -> ExitPlanMode skip with a short reminder. The check is anchored to the current plan session: a first pass finds where plan mode was (re-)entered — an EnterPlanMode tool call, or a genuine transition into plan read from a real user message's own permissionMode field (the reliable signal for a manual shift+tab re-entry after a restart drops plan-mode state) — then a second pass walks back only to that boundary, so a deny never points at stale text from a previous plan session or from before a restart. Crucially, a bare permission-mode:plan marker seen WHILE ALREADY in plan is ignored, not treated as a boundary: Claude Code writes one at essentially every plan-mode turn boundary, and the old logic mistook those for a fresh re-entry and false-blocked the compliant briefed-then-replied flow whenever a routine marker sat between the reply and the exit. Fail-open on any uncertainty, so it never deadlocks. When finding the user's reply it ignores entries that are not messages (only `type` exactly user or assistant counts, so stored API payloads such as api-request-blob and markers are skipped), subagent (isSidechain) entries, injected entries (isMeta) and compaction summaries, user entries whose origin is not human, and command, local-command and interrupt entries; a prompt the user typed while the agent's turn was running (written as a queued_command attachment, origin human) counts as a reply. Output: when it has verified a genuine user reply after the briefing it emits an explicit permissionDecision "allow" so the plan dialog passes once the user has replied — this is the ONE deliberate explicit allow in the whole plugin, on ExitPlanMode only, and a deny from any other hook still wins; every other pass (no transcript, parse error, no identifiable plan session, any uncertainty) emits nothing, so the user's own permission rules still apply; a skipped briefing writes the deny JSON. Reads the transcript only; writes nothing anywhere. (2) SessionStart on startup/resume — injects a short reminder (session-start-skill-reminder.js) to load and use the spec-driven-development skill for any code work. Static context injection, no project detection: the reminder itself states the 'if this is a code project' condition and lets the agent judge. Writes nothing. (3) PreToolUse on SendMessage - executor context checkpoint: a subagent is resumed by messaging it, so this is the one moment a hook can put a fact in front of the resume decision. It resolves the target agent id to that subagent's own transcript, reads the tail for the last usage record, and treats cache_read + cache_creation + input as the session's current context size. At 300K it notes that the ceiling is near; from 400K it says the session should be retired. It emits additionalContext and nothing else - no permissionDecision on either band - so the call always passes through untouched and the hook can never block, prompt, or alter it. THE AXIS CHANGED IN 1.22.0: the first version counted resumes and spoke at #15/#25. That worked in the narrow sense (the 105- and 119-resume tail vanished within a day) but measured the wrong thing - cost and defocus track context size, not resume count, and bounded dispatches continued by resume are the prescribed shape, so the old axis would have fired on exactly the behaviour the skill now asks for. Executors were measured at a median peak of 461K and as high as 997K, with 151 compact_boundary markers across the subagent transcripts: past that the harness autocompacts the executor, which then works from a lossy summary of its design basis. 400K is enforced by RETIREMENT, not compaction - it sits far below the ~930K compaction point, so a session retired on time is never compacted, and a fresh spawn re-reads the authoritative docs from disk while a compacted session keeps only a paraphrase. Complements (4), which bounds one dispatch from inside the executor; this one bounds accumulation across dispatches, which (4) cannot see. Deliberately not a gate: whether the session holds tacit knowledge a fresh spawn would lose is visible only to the main agent. Reviewer sessions are not exempt. Fail-open on everything - a `to` that is not a subagent id (a peer session or teammate name), an absent or unreadable subagent transcript, a parse error, or no usage record yet. Reads stdin + transcripts only (tail only); writes nothing. (4) PreToolUse matcher `*` - dispatch checkpoint (hooks/dispatch-checkpoint.js): fires INSIDE an executor's own session (agent_id is present only for subagent calls, so the main thread is never addressed) and, every time the dispatch passes the per-agent threshold, injects one note asking the executor to SendMessage a short status to "main" and CARRY ON WORKING - it stops nothing, truncates nothing and waits for nothing. Replaces the per-agent maxTurns ceilings removed in 1.24.0, which bought the same look at work in progress by cutting mid-action: a half-edited tree, a stale progress file and a blind resume, with the same turns re-paid afterwards. Both halves are measured: 62 of 62 subagent sends to "main" returned "Message queued for the main conversation's next turn", and 2,815 messages have reached executors mid-dispatch (delivered between turns, prefixed "The coordinator sent a message while you were working"), so the arbiter can correct direction where the executor stands. Thresholds are the measured per-dispatch medians keyed on agent_type (implementer 45, implementation-reviewer 40, design-reviewer/researcher 30, author 25, tester/verifier 20, tasks-design-verifier 15); the count is tool_use turns since the previous checkpoint or the dispatch boundary, whichever is nearer, so the note repeats every threshold and resets on resume. It NEVER tells the executor to read less - a dispatch spent reading reports what it learned (review-protocol.md, 'Progress reports arrive mid-dispatch'). Fail-open on the main thread, an unknown agent type, an unreadable transcript or a parse error; reads stdin + its own transcript tail, writes nothing. (5) PreToolUse on the spawn tool, matcher `Agent|Task` - approval gate (hooks/approval-gate.js): no spec-implementer or spec-tester dispatch before the user has approved something in this session, because code is the one thing Plan Mode protected and those two agents are the skill's code-writing delegates (the gate covers those two dispatches; other paths are governed by the skill's rules). Spec Mode no longer uses the harness Plan Mode (its planning is a workflow phase in an ordinary session, so roadmap writes, Artifact publishing and subagents writing the plan file all work), so the old read-only guarantee is replaced by this structural gate. Every other subagent type passes untouched (accepting both `spec-driven-development:spec-implementer` and the bare name). The gate does not bind the approval to a plan or spec: it never reads the dispatch prompt, and it verifies that the user replied, not what the reply said. Approval evidence is read from the session transcript and is either (1) an ExitPlanMode call whose tool_result is not an error (a rejection and a call the briefing checkpoint denied both come back as errors), or (2) a Bash or PowerShell call running scripts/approve.mjs <label> (the label is a free-form record: feature name, plan path or slug; the command must really run it, so `node ... approve.mjs <label>` has to start a command, at the start of the command string or after a newline, `;`, `&&` or `||`, and text that only mentions it inside quotes, after `#` or behind a literal `false &&` is not a call) made as the first action after the user's reply to a briefing - the path for Spec Mode and for a Quick Fix where the user left plan mode with shift+tab and replied (the same walk as (1), applied twice: the agent's mechanical tool turns, tool_result deliveries and injected entries are skipped, the first remaining message before the call must be a human reply, and the first remaining message before that reply must be the agent's own text, the briefing; a human message with no agent text before it, such as a session's first message, is not a reply, and agent text between the reply and the call voids the evidence; a prompt the user typed while the agent's turn was running, which Claude Code writes as a queued_command attachment, counts as a reply; slash-command entries do not). Evidence is void when a plan-mode entry occurs after it - an EnterPlanMode call (one the user declined, which comes back as an error, is not an entry), or a real user message whose permissionMode moves into plan - and the most recent valid evidence wins. Accepted cost: within a session an approval stays valid until the next plan-mode entry. approve.mjs writes nothing - it validates that a label is present and prints one line, and the call itself, recorded in the transcript, is the approval record; the main agent runs it only in the turn that answers the user's explicit confirmation of the final Spec Briefing (end of /create-spec or /update-spec), of the /implement condensed briefing, or of a Quick Fix briefing after the user left plan mode manually; the planning-phase Plan Briefing approves only the direction and does not trigger it. No evidence denies with a short reason saying how to get it: give the briefing as the turn-final message, wait for the user, run approve.mjs <label> as the first action (an approved ExitPlanMode already counts), then dispatch. Fail-open on any uncertainty (no or unreadable transcript, parse error, missing fields, a call from inside a subagent), so it can never deadlock; headless `claude -p` has no human reply to wait for, so the gate denies there by design. The transcript helpers it shares with (1) live in hooks/lib/transcript.js. Resumes go through SendMessage, not the spawn tool, so they are not gated - the original spawn was, and a resumed session continues work that was already approved. Reads stdin + the transcript only; writes nothing anywhere.
